question: For each customer and each month of 2020, first calculate the month-end balance by adding all deposit amounts and subtracting all withdrawal amounts that occurred during that specific month. Then determine which month in 2020 has the highest count of customers with a positive month-end balance and which month has the lowest count. For each of these two months, compute the average month-end balance across all customers and provide the difference between these two averages
sql:
-- Identify the month with highest positive_count and month with lowest positive_count
-- Then compute the difference between their average balances
WITH monthly_balances AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        SUBSTR(txn_date, 1, 7) as month,
        SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount 
            WHEN txn_type = 'withdrawal' THEN -txn_amount 
            ELSE 0 END) as month_end_balance
    FROM customer_transactions
    WHERE txn_date >= '2020-01-01' AND txn_date <= '2020-12-31'
    GROUP BY customer_id, SUBSTR(txn_date, 1, 7)
),
monthly_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        month,
        SUM(CASE WHEN month_end_balance > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as positive_count,
        AVG(month_end_balance) as avg_balance
    FROM monthly_balances
    GROUP BY month
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT 
        month,
        positive_count,
        avg_balance,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY positive_count DESC) as rank_highest,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY positive_count ASC) as rank_lowest
    FROM monthly_stats
)
SELECT 
    (SELECT avg_balance FROM ranked WHERE rank_highest = 1) as highest_avg_balance,
    (SELECT avg_balance FROM ranked WHERE rank_lowest = 1) as lowest_avg_balance,
    (SELECT avg_balance FROM ranked WHERE rank_highest = 1) - (SELECT avg_balance FROM ranked WHERE rank_lowest = 1) as difference
